spec: 21 §6 (ModelConfig v1 layout), 21 §6.1 (representation and canonical JSON, modelConfigSha256), 21 §6.3 (defaults), 21 §3 CI item 6, 21 §1.1 (effective ModelConfig), 21 §8 C4, 13 §7.3 (execution object, compat values), 12 §4.5 (clock), 14 §9 (feeds), 12 §8 (risk defaults), 12 §6.3 (runner), 11 §13.4 (rules)
notes: Canonical JSON (21 §6.1): keys sorted bytewise at every level, array order kept, no whitespace; modelConfigSha256 = sha256 of the canonical UTF-8 bytes. Values are only strings, booleans, safe integers, objects and arrays; money, sizes and ratios are decimal strings matching ^-?(0|[1-9][0-9]*)(\.[0-9]*[1-9])?$ with at most 6 fractional digits; other strings printable ASCII without `"` or `\`; keys ASCII; no floats.

The `ts_compat_default_*` vectors build the ts-compat default ModelConfig from the spec text alone. Every result-affecting field is pinned by the spec, but three UNUSED fields that still enter the hash are not fully fixed by the spec text: execution.latency.components (the values of the uncalibrated-2026-10 set are only shown as an example in 13 §7.3), execution.makerQueue (example values) and compatLatency.jitterMs (13 §7.4 says 0/0, 21 §6.3 says the built-in default is 0 / 20). The committed defaults file native/contract/defaults/model-config-v1.json is authoritative (21 §6.3); these vectors therefore test the CANONICALIZATION AND HASH FUNCTION on a spec-shaped object, and pin the sha only under the stated assumptions. D58 (A-01): the committed ts-compat default keeps compatLatency 0/0 (vector ts-compat-default-jitter0 is the spec-shaped candidate; CI item 6 pins the committed file, D57), the producer fallback of 21 §6.3 stays 0/20 for fresh submissions, the binary accepts any jitterMs >= 0 in ts-compat and zero jitter is enforced by the parity harness only.
Both hashes were computed with two independent implementations (Python hashlib and src/sha256.rs).

vectors.spec: 21 §6.1 (bytewise, not locale: digits < uppercase < underscore < lowercase)

vectors.assumption: execution.latency.components and makerQueue take the 13 §7.3 example values; compatLatency.jitterMs = 0 (13 §7.4, OR-6)

vectors.note: D58: the committed default is the jitter-0 variant; this one is the producer fallback shape of 21 §6.3 and only documents that the unused field changes the hash

vectors.statement: each candidate's modelConfigSha256 is the hash of run.modelConfig with execution replaced by the candidate's complete execution object when non-null; echo.modelConfigSha256 is the run-level hash; with execution: null both are equal

vectors.spec: 21 §6.1 (no floats; strings printable ASCII without quote or backslash; keys ASCII)

float where a safe integer is required
seed is a JSON integer (21 §6.2), not a string
ts-compat requires the compat axis values (13 §7.3) -> invalid_input
realistic with reports: compat requires sellGate: Matched (13 §7.3)
ts-compat clock delay must be constant 0 (12 §4.5)
